plugins.name: Agenda
plugins.summary: Your calendar on the HUD, walked with the ring.
plugins.description: The calendars your phone already syncs, on the glasses: what is next first, then the event's participants and its full description, paged for the HUD. Read-only and fully operable with the R08 ring.
plugins.author: beyondlevi

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Agenda puts the calendars your phone already syncs on the Rokid glasses. Nothing to configure beyond a permission: Google, Exchange/Outlook, CalDAV and local calendars all arrive through the phone's calendar provider, and nothing ever leaves the phone.

- **The list leads with what is next.** Title, start time on the right (`now` while it runs, `all day` for a full-day entry), and the day, the end and the location underneath. A running or imminent event takes the brightest row tone; later days are dimmed.
- **All-day and multi-day entries are context, not commitments.** Holidays, vacations and "away" blocks sort after the day's real meetings instead of holding the top of the list for weeks.
- **One appointment, one row.** The same meeting mirrored into a second calendar (a work account plus its Outlook copy) is collapsed, keeping the copy that carries the location and notes.
- **Participants.** The guest list of the open event, organiser first, RSVP on the right, declined guests dimmed. Invitations that carry only an address get a readable name.
- **Notes.** The whole description as a native reader document — no line clamp, no pages, scrolled by the glasses themselves and opened at its first line, with the calendar's HTML and decorative rules stripped.
- **One axis, four verbs.** Forward and back move, a tap opens, a double tap goes back. The row a tap would open carries a mark and the footer names it.
- Settings on the phone: the horizon (1/3/7/14/30 days), all-day events, hiding events you declined, and which calendars to include.

Requests only the `surfaces` capability. Calendar access is read-only.

Available in English and Portuguese; pick either in Android's per-app language settings, independently of the phone's language.

releases.notes:
- The event description is now a native **reader surface**: no three-line clamp, no pages, up to 40,000 characters, opened at its first line. The glasses own the wrapping and the scrolling.
- The document is budgeted in serialized bytes against both platform ceilings (the 64 KiB payload limit and the control-channel link), the shell is measured rather than assumed, and a description that had to be cut delivers its beginning plus a closing note.
- Requires glasses hub 1.4.3 or newer, which is where a reader page can open at the top of a document instead of its end.
- Built against bus-client sdk-v0.15.0.

### Artifact

- File: `agenda-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `708b7e96bdc3bd65d16adf45e48d62183db40520afbf59b16eabcf4960c50bae`

- The plugin now declares the languages it ships (`localeConfig`), so Agenda appears in Android's per-app language picker with English and Portuguese, independently of the phone's language. English is the default and the fallback for every other locale.

### Artifact

- File: `agenda-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `21432a21d7747c458c4bcc744b82758e4787dc8a99752716bb3b5c8c4f2d8616`

- First Nexus Store release of the Agenda plugin.
- Agenda list, event detail, participants and a paged description, all operable with the R08 ring one-axis method.
- Reads the phone's calendar provider read-only; no network and no account of its own.
- Rows are sized to what the HUD actually renders: a list-row title is one line, prose is cut by wrapped lines so no text is silently clipped.
- Duplicated (mirrored) appointments are collapsed into a single row.

### Artifact

- File: `agenda-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `e64ae01d10c26232a708f1d509a27cb0c1777827b95df79ba5b85b9cb8f6c56e`

plugins.name: Assistant
plugins.summary: The assist gesture, answered by the AI of your choice.
plugins.description: Press the assist gesture and ask out loud: the answer streams onto the glasses and is spoken aloud. Ride your own ChatGPT plan, or bring a key for OpenAI, OpenRouter, MiniMax, DeepSeek, GLM, Hermes, or any OpenAI-compatible server. It can see what you see, take notes and set reminders, keep the conversation going, and search the web when it needs to.
plugins.author: Anezium

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Press the assist gesture and ask out loud. The stock Rokid assistant window is closed for you the moment it appears; your words transcribe live in a band on the HUD, the answer streams into the same band, and then it is spoken aloud. No window to navigate — you ask, you hear, you keep walking.

## The AI of your choice

Sign in with ChatGPT and answers come from your own ChatGPT plan — nothing to paste, no per-token bill. Pick the model, from fastest to deepest, and how long it may think.

Or bring a key: OpenAI, OpenRouter, MiniMax (a Coding Plan key works as-is), DeepSeek, GLM (Z.ai), your own Hermes API server, or any OpenAI-compatible server of your own. Every provider keeps its own key — encrypted on the phone — its own model, and its own endpoint, so switching is one tap. Type any model id your provider serves, and a Personality box holds your standing instructions whoever answers.

Signed into ChatGPT, the assistant can also carry the memories and custom instructions of your account, so it starts out knowing what ChatGPT knows — with every provider. Synced automatically, and it can be turned off.

## It can look

Ask about what is in front of you and the model takes one photo through the glasses camera. One photo per question, only when the question needs eyes — asking for the weather will never fire the shutter — and never saved to the glasses' own gallery.

## Notes, reminders and timers

Ask it to remind you in twenty minutes, to set a timer, or to take a note, and it does — out loud, mid-sentence. When a reminder comes due the phone notifies you and the glasses raise it, waking the display if it went dark; away from the glasses, the phone still tells you. Everything lands in a Notes & reminders screen where you can read a note in full, delete one, or cancel a reminder before it rings. It stays on your phone, and it survives a reboot.

## Conversations

A follow-up keeps its context instead of starting over, and a thread ends on its own after a quiet delay you choose. The phone keeps the transcripts — with the photos, if you want them kept — in a Conversations screen where each can be read, and deleted, one by one or all at once.

## Web search

Built in. The model decides when a question needs the web, so news and weather are answerable from your face.

## What it keeps

Sign-in tokens are stored encrypted on the phone. Conversations, their photos and your memory text live in the plugin's private storage, never in your gallery, and are deleted the moment you ask.

## Needs

A ChatGPT account (or an OpenAI API key), plus *Show on your glasses*, *Glasses microphone*, *Speech to text*, *Text to speech*, *Replace the glasses assistant* and *Glasses camera* in Nexus → Settings → Plugin access. Requires Rokid Nexus 1.2.0.

releases.notes:
- **Hermes draws the cards now.** A weather question through a Hermes backend came back as plain text while the same model on any other provider drew the card. The seven bounded templates — weather, charts, metrics, rankings, comparisons, schedules and steps — now travel the same plain-text bridge as the other phone tools. Freeform Ink pages remain out of it.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `eda8b146e57a08dd997eb335fb72e44dd14da30189f470de91e35d741c4f092a`

- **Reminders, notes, timers and the calendar now work on Hermes too.** A server that runs its own tools never hands one back to the phone, so the assistant asks for a Nexus phone tool in plain text and Nexus runs it — the same tools every other provider gets, Ink pages aside.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `83b2a4083a0c85c5c02e75f2752c26ba35ba638c7cc0ac1a2f3d611916e67a1a`

- **Hermes is a provider of its own.** Give Settings the `/v1` root of your Hermes API server and its key, and the assistant answers from it — camera included: a server that runs its own tools still gets to look through the glasses.
- One conversation is now one Hermes session, from the first question to the last, instead of a fresh session for every sentence.
- An existing **Custom** connection recognises itself as Hermes when the server says so; a plain OpenAI-compatible server is left exactly as it was.
- Conversations can now stay open for seven days before starting fresh.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `bf927164812152b7c636afdf5d2eac51da4c39694edf055b3e68833faf5fb63b`

- **Your phone calendar is a real tool too.** Ask the assistant to add an appointment, read what is coming up, or delete one by its exact title and start time. Ambiguous matches and recurring series are refused instead of guessed.
- **Answers can become native interactive pages.** The assistant can author a strict Ink page, or pick one of seven bounded templates, for results that benefit from layout, charts, progress, or an action. The same phone compiler, native glasses renderer, typed limits and `ink_surface` grant used by public plugins apply; plain text and card answers remain the fallback.
- **The answer no longer goes dark during handover.** Listening, processing, and the final card or Ink page now share one display episode, whose scoped wake lock survives the band-to-surface morph and is released when that episode actually ends.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `b92e13a52e1a87a0baf1b3f4929bc7d20bf65e32dba323e011c57aac830593cc`

- **Ask it to remember, and it will.** Say "remind me in twenty minutes to check the oven", "set a timer for ten minutes", or "take a note that the spare key is under the pot" — the assistant schedules it, and at the moment it comes due your phone notifies you and the glasses raise the reminder, waking the display if it went dark. If the glasses are away, the phone still tells you and the reminder waits on the HUD for your return.
- It can also list what is pending, cancel a reminder by name, and search your notes back — all out loud, mid-conversation.
- **Notes & reminders**, a new section in settings, is where all of it lands: read a note in full, delete one, cancel a reminder before it rings. Nothing leaves the phone.
- Android guards precise alarms and notifications behind explicit consent, so the screen offers both — and only while something is actually missing. Without them a reminder still arrives, just later or only on the glasses; the assistant says so rather than pretending.
- Reminders survive a reboot, and one that came due while the phone was off is delivered once you turn it back on.
- **Every provider gets the new abilities**, not just ChatGPT: notes, reminders and timers are text, so a model that cannot see photos is no longer cut off from tools it could use perfectly well.
- Answers no longer show their formatting: models like to bold the time they just scheduled, and the glasses were rendering the asterisks.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `f8ecee3a016634318a402210a7f62259a8ff68e43d682a141a64c9da56b79500`

- **Every provider can look now.** Photo questions were a ChatGPT-only power; API providers were told they could look and could only pretend. Now a vision-capable model on MiniMax, OpenRouter, GLM, DeepSeek, or your own server takes a real photo through the glasses camera — same one-photo-per-question rule, same privacy: never saved to the glasses' gallery.
- A model that cannot see images is now told so and answers honestly, instead of inventing tool-call syntax in the middle of its reply. Set the "can see photos" switch for your model in the provider's settings to enable the camera.
- A server that does not understand tools is retried once without them, so plain custom endpoints keep answering as before.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `fd7889a7e0996ebc058c4e2ccf80afb90460ab48c6638d22f4f08cae583e1aa0`

- **No more thinking out loud.** Models that reason inline — MiniMax, GLM, DeepSeek and anything similar behind OpenRouter or a custom server — were showing their raw `<think>` traces in every answer. Those blocks are now stripped from the stream before the glasses display them, the voice reads them, or the conversation keeps them: only the answer itself gets through.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `cd512d4265e25306be26867bc2f5423bde47dec7f941bb7c8f03def4aecfef04`

- **Choose who answers.** Settings now opens on a provider list: your ChatGPT plan, an OpenAI key, OpenRouter, MiniMax (a Coding Plan key works as-is), DeepSeek, GLM (Z.ai), or any OpenAI-compatible server of your own. Each provider keeps its own key — encrypted on the phone — its own model choice, and its own endpoint, so switching is one tap, not a re-setup.
- **Any model id.** Pick from the suggestions or type the exact model your provider serves. For a model the app does not know, say whether it can see photos; photo questions are handled gracefully either way.
- **Give it a personality.** A new Personality box holds standing instructions — a persona, a tone, house rules — layered under the HUD formatting rules.
- Your notes and synced ChatGPT memories keep riding along with every question, whichever provider answers; the Memory toggle remains the single off switch.
- Signing out of ChatGPT no longer forgets the keys you saved for other providers.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `d0dfa744e92d4f9b3d25cee0e5d4e927bfdd908fb8208b7d8d1c931cdf088572`

- **Answers at full length.** The model is no longer told to stay under two short sentences: ask for detail and it answers as fully as the question deserves, in real paragraphs that the glasses render with hard line breaks instead of one flattened run of text. The notice band on the glasses grows and paginates to hold it.
- While you dictate, the band keeps showing the tail of what it heard rather than paginating your own words away mid-sentence.
- Requires Rokid Nexus 1.2.0 or newer on both the phone and the glasses.

### Artifact

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `b1306ddc08ac37e89a1247320217ef4e2f35e5d3527331e7103486a086d67578`

- First release: press the assist gesture, speak, and the answer streams onto the glasses. The stock Rokid assistant window is closed for you the moment it appears; your words transcribe live in a band on the HUD and the reply arrives in the same band, then is spoken aloud.
- **Sign in with ChatGPT.** Answers come from your own ChatGPT plan — nothing to paste, no per-token bill. An OpenAI API key works as the alternative route.
- **It can look.** Ask about what is in front of you and the model takes one photo through the glasses camera — one per question, only when the question needs eyes, and never saved to the glasses' own gallery.
- **Conversations continue.** A follow-up question keeps its context instead of starting over; a thread ends on its own after a quiet delay you choose. The phone keeps the transcripts — with the photos, if you want them kept — and both can be deleted at any time.
- **It starts out knowing you.** Memories and custom instructions from the ChatGPT account you signed in with are carried into the assistant, so you do not introduce yourself twice. Optional, synced automatically, and it can be turned off.
- **Web search built in.** The model decides when a question needs the web, so the weather and the news are answerable from your face.
- Pick the model (fastest to deepest) and how long it may think, in Settings.
- Requires Rokid Nexus 1.1.6 or newer, with *Show on your glasses*, *Glasses microphone*, *Speech to text*, *Text to speech*, *Replace the glasses assistant* and *Glasses camera* approved in Nexus → Settings → Plugin access.

- File: `assistant-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `571ab6f8a598f9146545cb4fdb80b1a24ac7408585cf8b9215c869450ec70443`

plugins.name: Home Assistant
plugins.summary: Home Assistant dashboards and controls on the glasses.
plugins.description: An unofficial community plugin that renders configurable Home Assistant pages on Rokid Nexus and runs the action assigned to the selected widget.
plugins.author: Zhilin

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Build pages from live Home Assistant values, buttons, toggles, status rows, and progress widgets, then browse and control them from the glasses. Priority-based context rules can select the most relevant page automatically.

The Home Assistant URL and long-lived access token are configured on the phone. The token is protected by Android Keystore and never enters a Nexus surface or glasses payload. The connection is active only while settings or a Nexus HUD session needs it.

## Unofficial integration

This is an unofficial community plugin. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Home Assistant project, Nabu Casa, or Rokid.

releases.notes:
- Add password-encrypted export and import for connection credentials and dashboard configuration.
- Include the Home Assistant URL, long-lived access token, Rokid token, pages, widgets, actions, value bindings, and context rules.
- Validate imported data before replacing the current credentials and dashboard.

- Replace the opinionated starter dashboard with a neutral setup guide.
- Remove legacy built-in starter pages and rules while preserving user-created pages.
- Keep the in-app unofficial community-plugin disclosure.
- Build against the latest published Nexus SDK (sdk-v0.15.0).

plugins.name: Lume
plugins.summary: Glanceable RSVP speed-reading on the HUD.
plugins.description: Read PDFs, TXT files and shared text one word at a time on the glasses, streamed from your phone. Adaptive pacing, adjustable speed, pause and sentence stepping, and per-document progress. Manage your library on the phone; read hands-free with the R08 ring.
plugins.author: beyondlevi

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Lume turns Rokid glasses into a wearable speed reader. It uses RSVP (Rapid Serial Visual Presentation): text flows one word at a time at a fixed point in your field of view, so your eyes never travel across a line.

- Import PDF/TXT, paste text, or share into Lume from any app (extraction stays on-device).
- Adaptive pacing: long words, clause/sentence endings and paragraph breaks hold longer.
- Adjustable speed (150-700 wpm), pause, and sentence stepping, all on the R08 ring.
- Per-document reading progress; resume where you left off.

Fully operable by the R08 Access Bridge one-axis ring: move to select, tap to open/play/pause, back to exit.

plugins.name: News
plugins.summary: RSS and Atom feeds on the HUD, read with the ring.
plugins.description: Subscribe to RSS or Atom feeds on the phone and read them on the glasses: sources with unread counts, headlines newest first, and the article text on the glasses' native reader surface. Fully operable with the R08 ring.
plugins.author: beyondlevi

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

News puts your RSS and Atom feeds on the Rokid glasses. Subscribe on the phone, then browse headlines and read articles on the HUD without touching anything but the ring.

- Three views on one axis: sources, headlines, reader. Forward/back moves, tap opens, double tap goes back.
- Headlines use both text bands of a list row, with age and source as trailing tokens; read items dim instead of disappearing.
- Article text is reduced to paragraphs on the phone and rendered on the glasses' native reader surface: continuous prose that the ring scrolls, opening on the first paragraph.
- Per-feed unread counts, cached articles between sessions, and a feed that fails to fetch keeps what it had.
- Add feeds by URL or from seven verified presets (BBC World, NYT World, Hacker News, Ars Technica, The Verge, G1, Tecnoblog); each feed names itself from its channel title on the first fetch.

Requests only the `surfaces` capability: feeds are fetched phone-side with the app's own HTTP stack.

releases.notes:
- Fixes from the Store's automated source review of 1.1.0.
- The control-only document is budgeted in UTF-8 bytes rather than characters, so a CJK or emoji article is no longer measured at a third of its real size and dropped by the hub.
- The closing note is reserved before the article text is laid in; it could previously push the document past the SDK's character limit, which throws inside the plugin's own process.
- Surface sends dedupe on the rendered document instead of the article id, so a feed that rewrites an open article now reaches the wearer instead of leaving stale text on screen.

### Requires

- Glasses hub 1.4.3 or newer (versionCode 10403).

### Artifact

- File: `news-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `5e0d97092c600e47cca7be86841813e4ec31a7e36cbbae42f970c697263d5de4`

- Articles now render on the glasses' native reader surface: the hub wraps and scrolls continuous prose, so an article arrives whole instead of being cut into viewport-sized pages. About 17 lines of text per screen instead of four clamped blocks.
- Forward/back scroll the document by viewport and back returns to the headline list.
- An article opens on its first paragraph, and a refresh never moves the wearer from where they were reading (`NexusReaderAnchor.TOP`).
- On a control-only link the document is trimmed to what the link can carry, with a note saying so, instead of failing to appear.

### Requires

- Glasses hub 1.4.3 or newer (versionCode 10403).

### Artifact

- File: `news-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `e72dc713c3f9e4dc67f1865a517fd77a7f8506fd8f8fa22f84275e93bb86c519`

- First Nexus Store release of the News RSS/Atom reader.
- Three HUD views - sources, headlines, reader - fully operable with the R08 ring one-axis method.
- Headlines read across both text bands of a list row, so roughly twice as much of each headline is legible.
- Article text is paged for the HUD and wrapped at the measured capacity of a prose row, so no sentence is clipped.
- Feeds are fetched by the phone with a hardened parser (no doctypes, no external entities, bounded input).

plugins.name: Photos Sync
plugins.summary: Glasses captures land in your phone gallery.
plugins.description: Photos and videos you take on the glasses copy themselves into your phone gallery, in the same Hi Rokid album. They travel over the Bluetooth connection the glasses already have, so neither device needs Wi-Fi.
plugins.author: Anezium

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Photos and videos you take on the glasses copy themselves into your phone gallery, in the same `Download/Hi Rokid/` album Hi Rokid imports into. They travel over the Bluetooth connection the glasses already have, so neither device needs Wi-Fi.

## Syncing

Choose when it runs: **always**, so a capture syncs as soon as you take it; **while charging**, the default, so transfers happen while the glasses rest on the charger; or **manual only**.

Every file is checksum-verified before it reaches your gallery, and an interrupted transfer resumes where it stopped instead of starting over — so a long video finishes across several sessions.

The transfer stays out of the way of everything else on the connection: it pauses for a camera session and yields whenever anything else needs the link.

## Freeing space

Deleting captures from the glasses once they are safely on the phone is available as an opt-in, off by default. Some glasses refuse it, and the screen says so rather than pretending.

releases.notes:
- **Choose which capture types sync.** Settings now lists photos, AR photos, videos and AR videos as separate switches, so a type you never want copied stops crossing the Bluetooth link at all instead of being deleted after the fact. Everything stays on by default.
- The screen also says plainly what a synced file will look like: AR overlays and video stabilization are added by the Hi Rokid app after its own import, so captures synced here arrive as the raw file — plain photos, and clips without stabilization. One line per type, next to its switch.

### Artifact

- File: `photosync-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `f75a41253b7eb7dcf71b7e51e9fb608c79d5204cdee3b8376f5745e5ddd1e917`

- The plugin's mark matches its Store icon again: the sync arrow is full size and crosses the frame, rather than sitting in a corner as decoration.

### Artifact

- File: `photosync-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `cceb8f91f955c4af52840961d4cdbd3a24ca27d0cc6bd6971f79ae095bf5bf67`

- A capture taken seconds ago is no longer skipped. A file still being written is not ready to copy, but the rest of the catalog is - so a fresh photo left the run eligible while its own bytes were still settling, and nothing came back for it. Scanning and settling are now separate decisions.
- The phone hub comes back on its own after a reboot or an app update, instead of waiting to be opened by hand while captures piled up on the glasses.
- Requires Rokid Nexus 1.1.0 or newer.

### Artifact

- File: `nexus-photosync-1.0.1.apk`
- SHA-256: `c54f859105398189744eb3b07e61d293244a627e616087c16b7c017137e461da`

- First release: glasses captures copy themselves into `Download/Hi Rokid/` on the phone, over Bluetooth — no Wi-Fi on either device.
- Three sync modes: always, while charging (default), or manual only.
- Interrupted transfers resume from where they stopped, and every file is checksum-verified before it reaches the gallery.

plugins.name: Relay
plugins.summary: Phone messages on your glasses, answered out loud.
plugins.description: A message you can reply to reaches the glasses as it arrives. Read it without taking the phone out, speak your answer, and it sends itself. Anything you miss waits for you in Messages.
plugins.author: Anezium

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

A message you can reply to reaches the glasses as it arrives, and lights the display if it was dark. You read it where you are already looking, answer out loud, and the phone stays in your pocket.

## Reading

Each message keeps its sender beside it, so a group conversation reads as a conversation rather than a wall of text. A long thread turns pages instead of stopping at eight lines.

*Message display time* in the plugin's settings is a number you type, 2 to 45 seconds, and *Longer for long messages* adds reading time per character on top for threads that need it.

## Privacy

In public or in a meeting, *Hide message text on the glasses* keeps the band to the sender's name and a Show chip — the words appear only when you tap for them, and Reply stays one tap away. *Hide previews in the inbox* does the same for the Messages list. While the band is hidden, read-aloud names the sender only.

## Answering

Speak your reply and it sends itself after a few seconds, counted down on the chip you are looking at — cancellable for its whole length, and never sent before you have seen what it heard. If the glasses went dark or lost the link, the clock stops and waits for you.

## Messages you missed

One you let go, or one that arrived while you were in another plugin, is in **Messages** in the Nexus menu: every conversation waiting on you, newest first, read and answered the same way. The list updates while you are looking at it.

## Hearing it instead

Turn on *Read notifications aloud* and the glasses speak the message as it arrives — the whole message, in the voice and at the speed you already chose in your Rokid assistant settings. It is produced on the glasses, so it works with the phone in your pocket and nothing leaves the device. Off by default.

## What it relays

Anything with a reply box, from any app. Nothing else, and nothing to tick first.

## What it keeps

Nothing. Messages live in memory while the plugin runs, are never written to disk, and never appear in a log. Revoke notification access and what it captured goes with it.

## Needs

Notification access on the phone, plus *Show on your glasses*, *Speech to text* and *Text to speech* in Nexus → Settings → Plugin access.

releases.notes:
- **The glasses can name who messaged without showing what.** Two new switches: *Hide message text on the glasses* keeps the band to the sender and a Show chip — tap it when the moment is right, and Reply is still one tap away — and *Hide previews in the inbox* keeps the list to names; opening a conversation still reads it. Read-aloud names the sender only while the band is hidden.
- **Message display time is now a number you type.** Two to 45 seconds, 3 by default, with a separate *Longer for long messages* switch that adds reading time per character. Existing settings carry over: Auto becomes 3 seconds with scaling on, a fixed value stays fixed.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `8b2fa6d329f59ca0b3a2f51591c5c07239c57b4cd07bf04bc9487c5dfc92468b`

- **A conversation from Messages now opens as a full-screen reader.** Instead of a band that paginates, the thread wraps as prose and scrolls in the native glasses renderer, so a long exchange reads like a page. Tapping still starts a reply, and Back still returns to the Messages list.
- **An open conversation stays live.** A message arriving while you are reading is added in place, keeping your scroll position, and without interrupting dictation, the review of a reply, or a send already counting down.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `ddb5c5bb813fdf6a0905583b6cda8111f271b6ab1689e1bd16989a4c0c689ea3`

- **After a reply is sent, the inbox comes back a bit sooner.** The "Sent" screen used to hand you back to the list after 1.2 seconds — which turned out to be the exact moment most people tap Back, so the tap landed on a list they had not seen yet and threw them out of Relay entirely. The hand-back now happens at 0.85 seconds: still enough to read "Sent", but the switch is over before your thumb gets there.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `6268b2f3867c956b9e16b8bfc5612ac3ed573faeafcd8820332bd5a78bd613fd`

- **Messages Android hides can now come through.** Since Android 15 the system blanks out any notification it reads as carrying a code — and it reads far more than real codes that way, so an ordinary message with a few digits in it arrived on the glasses as "Sensitive notification content hidden". The only exemption Android grants is to an app registered as a device's companion, which is exactly what Relay is, so a new **Show messages Android hides** entry under Access offers to register it with your glasses. It is off until you ask for it, and Android's own dialog tells you what registering covers before anything happens. The registration is worth having on its own: it also lets Relay keep running when the system would otherwise stop it, which is one of the ways a message used to go missing entirely.
- **When Android does hide a message, Relay now says so in its own words** instead of showing you the system's placeholder as though it were the message.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `bd73200282e03aaef4cd72e10758739539c53a0b08be153434add18c0abaf40d`

- **A message now waits for the glasses instead of being dropped after five seconds.** The link to the glasses drops and heals on its own all the time — a pocket, a doorway, standby — and healing routinely takes ten to thirty seconds. Relay used to give a captured message five seconds to reach the glasses and then silently gave up: the message sat in the inbox, and the band never came. A message now waits out the reconnection for up to two minutes and shows the moment the link is back. Relay also stopped trusting a "sent" that never left the phone, and transient hiccups during registration no longer throw the waiting message away. Pairs well with Rokid Nexus 1.2.8, which fixes a related blind spot on the glasses side for back-to-back messages.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `c378c901ae7aa9573effea3ef20776c0ddcc88e5fd3f9d6e95ed7fb2dcd100df`

- **Choose how long messages stay up.** Display time has always scaled with the length of the message, so a two-word text was gone in about four seconds — often before your hand reached the touchpad, let alone the Reply chip. A new *Message display time* stepper in the plugin's settings sets a fixed duration instead, from 5 to 45 seconds, applied to every message whatever its length. Auto, the default, keeps the scaling behavior unchanged.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `6196f4171745e929d6817f4f26cacb3148443b608850ab00a58d0cea0e197af0`

- **Read notifications aloud.** A new switch, off by default, has the glasses speak a message when it arrives — the newest message whole, not a preview. The band is held open while it reads and gives you the usual answering window once it stops. Answering interrupts the reading, and so does dictating. Needs Rokid Nexus 1.1.5; the speech is produced on the glasses, so nothing leaves the device.
- **"Sent" lands on the chip you were watching**, instead of confirming above a button still counting down to a send that already happened.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `8c380dd4610df0f6c6a4e35430fb96a7317768a57f460277820fec50655edf00`

- **Black out behind notifications.** A new switch, off by default, asks the glasses to hide everything else while a Relay notification is up — only the notification shows. Leaving it off keeps the band floating over whatever you were looking at. Needs Rokid Nexus 1.1.4; older hubs simply ignore the request.
- The test harness can crowd the inbox: an Eight threads button posts eight conversations at once, one more than the glasses list shows at a time.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `59104e1389207293374640f760476ca38faf5169dca8150ea6804a02cd9b4bf5`

- Relay has its own mark instead of the shared chat icon: two bubbles, the message that arrived and the answer going back. The same mark is now the app icon, so what you tap in the Store is what you find afterwards.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `95079f10de87ee4f7cd061cee51c24ad17c72f6724e50e99796f77528c2f4f03`

- First release: messages you can reply to reach the glasses as they arrive, and light the display if it was dark.
- Each message keeps its sender beside it, and a long conversation turns pages.
- Speak your reply and it sends itself after a few seconds, counted down where the answers are and cancellable for its whole length.
- Anything you missed waits in **Messages** in the Nexus menu, newest first, updating while you look at it.
- Nothing is stored: messages live in memory while the plugin runs and never reach disk or a log.
- Requires Rokid Nexus 1.1.0 or newer.

### Artifact

- File: `nexus-relay-1.0.0.apk`
- SHA-256: `619c5a912bb754849802c5aa6cb36b30593a64cc28592f1a6fdb5d07732bdd09`

plugins.name: RokidHub · Yandex
plugins.summary: Control Yandex Smart Home by voice from Rokid RV101.
plugins.description: An unofficial community plugin that listens through Nexus STT, controls Yandex Smart Home, and returns the result on the HUD and through Nexus TTS.
plugins.author: Azat Akhmetshin

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Control Yandex Smart Home from Rokid RV101 without saying the wake word “Alice”. Open **RokidHub · Yandex** from the Nexus launcher, speak a natural Russian command, and get the result on the HUD and through Nexus TTS.

Supported in the first release:

- turn devices on and off;
- ask for a temperature sensor reading;
- repeat a command with a tap while the plugin is open.

## Setup

Install the plugin on the Android phone, approve the `surfaces`, `stt`, and `tts` capabilities in Rokid Nexus, then open its settings and sign in with Yandex. Triple-tap the glasses touchpad to open the Nexus launcher.

## Privacy

In the recommended direct mode, sign-in uses the official Yandex LoginSDK. The OAuth token stays on the phone, encrypted by Android Keystore, and is sent only to the Yandex IoT API. It is not sent to RokidHub.

An optional cloud mode is disabled by default. It uses a separate revocable RokidHub installation credential; the plugin never receives the server-side Yandex OAuth token.

## Unofficial integration

This is an unofficial community project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Yandex, Rokid, or Anezium.

releases.notes:
- First public Rokid Nexus release.
- Voice on/off commands and temperature queries for Yandex Smart Home.
- Direct OAuth mode with Android Keystore protection.
- Optional separately revocable RokidHub cloud mode.

plugins.name: Tasker
plugins.summary: Run your Tasker automations from the glasses.
plugins.description: Your named Tasker tasks, listed on the glasses HUD. Swipe to the one you want, tap, and the phone runs it — lights, scenes, volumes, whatever you taught Tasker to do.
plugins.author: Anezium

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Every named task in your Tasker setup, listed on the glasses. Swipe through them, tap one, and the phone runs it where it stands — the glasses are the remote, Tasker does the work. Anything you can put in a task is now a glance and a tap away: toggle the lights, start a scene, silence the phone, log your coffee.

## On the glasses

Tasks appear under the project they belong to, in one list. Tap a task and the card answers with *Sent* once Tasker has taken the order; the list stays open, so firing two or three tasks in a row is just more taps. If something is missing — Tasker disabled, external access off, permission not granted — the card says exactly what, and the plugin's settings on the phone walk you through fixing it.

*Sent* means Tasker accepted the run. The card does not track what the task did afterwards — a task that itself fails does so on the phone, in Tasker's own logs.

## Needs

[Tasker](https://tasker.joaoapps.com/) installed on the phone with at least one named task, **Allow External Access** enabled in Tasker's preferences (Misc tab), and the Tasker run permission granted from the plugin's settings screen. On the Nexus side, only *Show on your glasses*.

releases.notes:
- Initial port of Tasker Bridge to the Nexus plugin platform: browse your named Tasker tasks on the glasses HUD and run one with a tap. The old app's custom transport (BLE wake, RFCOMM bridge, CXR-L helper APK) is gone — the Nexus bus carries everything.

- SHA-256: `6e4d17551030f0c15d8f6c2a9e181f9b4b51166d8858d720aac0fab3c67fe2d2`

## About

plugins.name: Tuya Smart Home
plugins.summary: Your Tuya / Smart Life home on the HUD, walked with the ring.
plugins.description: The homes, rooms and devices of your Tuya / Smart Life account on the glasses: pick a home, pick a room, pick a device, and act on its own datapoints. Switches toggle in place, modes open a value list, temperature and brightness open a stepper. Fully operable with the R08 ring.
plugins.author: beyondlevi

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Tuya Smart Home brings the smart-home account you already use on your phone to the Rokid glasses. It walks the same hierarchy the Smart Life app does — **home, room, device** — and then shows the device's real datapoints, read from the device itself rather than from a fixed list of supported models.

- **Every control is typed from the device.** A boolean datapoint becomes a switch that flips on tap; an enum opens its declared options; an integer opens a stepper clamped to the range and step the device reports. Sensors and other reported-only values are shown dimmed, so it is obvious what can be acted on.
- **Infrared air conditioners work.** IR bridges accept one set of codes and report another (`switch` versus `power`, `fan` versus `wind`); the plugin resolves them onto each other instead of showing an empty state.
- **Shared homes degrade honestly.** Tuya only serves the room list to a home's owner, so a home you merely administer is shown as a single flat device list rather than failing.
- **One axis, always.** Forward and back move the selection, tap acts, double tap goes up a level — nothing needs a pointer, a gesture or a second axis.

## Setup

Create a cloud project on [iot.tuya.com](https://iot.tuya.com), link the Smart Life account to it, and paste the **Access ID** and **Access Secret** into the plugin's settings along with the project's data center. A *Test connection* button reports how many homes and devices the project can actually see, and the account UID is resolved automatically.

The plugin talks to the Tuya cloud from the phone. It requests only the `surfaces` capability — no microphone, no camera.

## Privacy

Your Tuya keys are stored on the phone, in the plugin's own private storage, and are sent to nothing but Tuya's API.

releases.notes:
- The Tuya Access Secret is no longer written to a plaintext preferences file. Credentials now live in `EncryptedSharedPreferences`, sealed with an AES key held in the Android Keystore; a store written by 1.0.0 is migrated on first launch and then deleted. If the Keystore is unavailable the plugin fails closed and asks for the keys again rather than falling back to plaintext.
- Network responses are bounded (2 MiB) and rejected before parsing, and every call carries a whole-call timeout alongside the connect/read ones.
- Leaving a screen while it is still loading now abandons that request; a reply landing after BACK could previously reopen the screen the wearer had just left.

### Artifact

- File: `tuya-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `dc058c4bf60cb57d905e867d7cd6b111dd58f10ccb120f788fbdedbf6b3c1538`

- First release. Homes → rooms → devices → device controls on the glasses HUD, driven entirely by the R08 one-axis input (NEXT / PREV / SELECT / BACK).
- Tuya Cloud client with HMAC-SHA256 request signing, token refresh and per-region endpoints.
- Datapoint typing: boolean switches toggle in place, enums open a value list, integers open a range-clamped stepper, reported-only datapoints render dimmed.

plugins.name: Wireless ADB
plugins.summary: Put the glasses on ADB over Wi-Fi, without a cable.
plugins.description: Turn on Android's real wireless debugging on the glasses and get a pairing code with the exact adb pair and adb connect commands to run from your computer. No cable, no Settings automation, no Accessibility.
plugins.author: Anezium

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

The glasses have no USB port you would want to use for this. Wireless ADB turns on Android's own wireless debugging transport on them and hands you the two commands to paste — `adb pair` with a fresh code, then `adb connect` — so a computer on the same network is talking to the glasses in under a minute.

It does not drive the Settings app and it does not use Accessibility. The plugin sends typed requests through Nexus; the phone hub checks the signer-bound *Wireless debugging* grant and stamps the plugin's identity, and the glasses hub performs only the fixed system operations involved: trust the current Wi-Fi network, start pairing, cancel pairing, disable ADB.

## Using it

Approve **Wireless debugging** in Nexus plugin access, open the plugin's settings, and tap **Enable & pair computer**. If the glasses' Wi-Fi radio is off, Nexus turns it on and waits for a saved network first — it does not choose or configure one for you. Run the `adb pair` command it shows, then the `adb connect` command, from your computer.

**Disable wireless debugging** closes the transport when you are done. It disables ADB only, and leaves the glasses on their normal Wi-Fi network.

## About the code

The pairing code lives for two minutes and is never logged or written to disk — after a hub restart only the service name and the expiry deadline survive, enough to close the window but not to reopen it. **Copy command** deliberately puts the command, code included, on the Android clipboard: clear it afterwards if your phone syncs its clipboard elsewhere. While a code is on screen the settings window blocks screenshots and screen recording.

If the pairing window cannot be closed the normal way, Nexus disables wireless debugging outright; if that fails too, it keeps showing the window as open and retries, rather than telling you it is closed.

## Needs

Rokid Nexus 1.4.1 or newer on both the phone and the glasses, installed through their normal signed upgrade path, with *Wireless debugging* approved in Nexus → Settings → Plugin access. A saved Wi-Fi network on the glasses, developer access already set up, and a computer on the same LAN. The validated Rokid Android 12L (API 32) firmware — other API levels fail closed.

releases.notes:
- First release: enable Android's wireless debugging transport on the glasses without a cable and without automating Settings. The plugin creates a two-minute pairing code and shows the exact `adb pair` and `adb connect` commands to run from a computer on the same network, and can cancel an open pairing window or disable the transport again.
- **Enable & pair restores Wi-Fi when it needs to.** If the glasses' Wi-Fi radio is off, Nexus turns it on and waits for a saved network before enabling ADB, instead of failing on a radio it could have switched on.
- **Disable stays scoped to ADB.** It closes wireless debugging without disconnecting the glasses from the network they were using.
- The code is never logged or persisted, and the settings window blocks screenshots and screen recording while it is visible.
- Requires Rokid Nexus 1.4.1 or newer on the phone and the glasses, and the validated Rokid Android 12L (API 32) firmware.
